title: Swarmbly AI 3.5.1: privacy, team and recipe fixes
description:
Version 3.5.1 fixes what the sealed bank v5 found in 3.5.0, with SwarmblyApp 0.8.1. Bank v5 measured 3.5.0 once (two banks, 32 cards × 3 repetitions, two-node mode, qwen2.5:7b, an isolated judge): the circle, permission and honest-team criteria were met; zero unauthorised sends was not met (a proposed public query kept the distinctive word of a private name, or the definition of a private glossary term), and exact results with code stayed far below 90 %. Version 3.5.1 removes private names in every form, keeps the public entity whole and in order, marks a team step complete only when it produced output, asks for thinking only when the model supports it, runs recipe 5 in /data with a writable scratch /tmp, raw CSV samples and partial output flagged, and makes the list preview sensitive for private terms. Benchmark harness 1.4.5. The fixes were measured on open batteries with a real model (no private term sent; code 31/39 against 25/39 on 3.5.0), the team-versus-local battery ran once on one computer, the deterministic node-loss battery passes, and a non-blind repeat of bank v5.2 sent no private name. The blind measurement is a new sealed bank, v6, run once on this release.

Version 3.5.0 was the software for the private beta: teams and trusted circles. Trusted circles with signed membership manifests and invitations by code or QR, checked at the handshake and at the worker gate; the circle as a destination class, so every send to a peer goes through the destination policy and the receipt names the circle; work beyond the local network through the circle's own relay (a new prototype), with a pinned certificate, the nodes' TLS end to end through the relay, and the owner pushing each signed manifest version so that a revocation takes effect at once; node roles (large model, reasoner, and opt-in search and corpus executors); teams as stored plan templates with honest partial results (complete, partial or failed; dependent steps blocked, never guessed); reciprocity credits as signed, non-transferable receipts, offered only to a busy worker, with double spends detected by the issuer; the code sandbox prepared at first launch with a 4 GiB memory floor and an explicit override; a doctor export built from an allow-list; release artifacts with SHA-256 checksums and Sigstore keyless signatures; a beta kit; and batteries for team versus local and node loss with a guide for sealed bank v5. Everything was built and tested on loopback with canned models. Nothing in this version was measured with real models, between real machines on different networks or on a sealed bank; the beta's exit criteria (team versus local, node loss, successful installs, no severe bug for two weeks) and sealed bank v5 are measured during the beta and published as they are.

Version 3.4.0 adds tools and data with code. One tool broker with the destination policy and the receipt; an MCP client with approval per call (a local tool may be set to "don't ask again in this project", remote tools, the sandbox and author search always ask); skills in the open Agent Skills format (SKILL.md), instructions only; author search with consent (ORCID, OpenAlex, PubMed); recipe 4, a list on the swarm; recipe 5, data with code in a WASI sandbox (wasi-python 0.1.5, no network, writes only to /out); the Anthropic provider, an embeddings role, the swarmbly-agent 0.1.0 runtime and Python 3.11 as the minimum; private glossary entries. The sealed banks v4.1 and v4.2 were run once: seal OK, 0 technical failures and all eight permission counters at 0, but a public query proposed by the App kept a fragment of a private name (one card in v4.1, two in v4.2, three repetitions each), so zero unauthorised sends is not met, and exact results in código-exacto stayed below 90 % (0/9 and 6/12); the permissions were not widened by data and the sandbox held. The fixes after the run (private names removed whole and by distinctive word with the removed terms shown, text documents in recipe 5, relevant passages per item in the list recipe, private glossary entries) were measured only on open batteries (recipe 4 30/36 cases and 195/201 cells; recipe 5 39/39 cases and 57/57 numbers; v4 self-test 24/24; 0 unauthorised sends); a new sealed bank will confirm them.

Version 3.3.0 adds models by role and a start screen, "What do you want to do?", with three recipes run as flows in code: ask your documents; compare documents in a table built by code from the values each document supports (source tables, also turned, CSV files, sentences with one value per place, corrected values marked, differences computed by code); and research with public sources, where the query is proposed without the user's private names, codes or figures and nothing leaves until the user approves it, the documents and the results are labelled apart, and comparisons and disagreements between them are computed by code. A claim verifier checks every labelled sentence against the paragraph it cites. Every step was measured on two open, fictitious batteries (final runs 112/123 and 48/57 cases, no leak). Measured once on two new sealed banks: no passage or personal name sent and the app's receipt matching the observed traffic in 56/56 cases, but in two cases a private site name left in a query the harness approved as proposed, fixed after the run; compositions still fail the banks' strict rubric (0/16). Confirmation runs of the same banks are not blind and are reported apart. The usability test of the receipt with people is postponed.

Version 3.2.0 makes compositions say where their figures come from and adds two privacy fixes. Citation labels are attached by code where every figure of an unlabelled sentence is found in a paragraph of the user's documents; the facts of the sources that a composition leaves out are shown under it and, when they are of the same kind as one the answer gives, closed with one short paragraph; sources that disagree are shown side by side; documents named by their file come first; an optional larger local model can write compositions. Ollama cloud models are treated as third parties, and instructions written inside a user's document are marked and never followed. Every step was measured on an open, fictitious development battery before it was kept; steps that did not help with a 7B model (a requirement list, a bounded self-repair, lexical scaffolding) stay off. Measured with two sealed banks: claims in compositions backed by a citation rose from 10/69 to 22/59 and from 8/53 to 21/61, with no regression in personal-data questions, no forbidden send, and the app's receipt matching the observed network traffic in 24/24 cases; no composition passes its rubric yet (the work of 3.3).

Version 3.1.0 adds projects (a folder of its own per piece of work, with its documents, memory and conversations, isolated and exportable as a verified package), citations that name the paragraph of the user's document and survive moving the folder, memory that keeps only what the user confirms (notes and glossary entries from requests, definitions and corrections), online search only when the user approves the exact text, search terms reviewed as concepts (glossary, Wikidata, GBIF), consent per question for public lookups, and answers that mark sentences presented as sourced but without a citation. Measured with two sealed banks: no forbidden send in 17/17 personal-data cases and 7/7 compositions, the app's receipt matched the observed network traffic in 24/24 cases, and citation-backed claims in compositions rose over every earlier version; no composition passes its rubric yet (the work of 3.2).

Version 3.0.1 added a destinations policy (every model server, public source and peer is classified as this computer, the user's own network or a third party, and an outbound policy runs before every call), a privacy receipt with every answer built from what was actually sent, API keys in the system keychain, a Docker distribution and a blind benchmark harness for sealed question banks. Measured with two sealed banks: no forbidden send in 17/17 personal-data cases, and the app's receipt matched the observed network traffic in 23/24 cases (the remaining case was fixed after the measurement and verified by tests).

Swarmbly AI is a decentralized, local-first AI system that splits the problem rather than the model. A local orchestrator keeps personal and sensitive work on the user's computer and sends public, decomposable work once to volunteer nodes running complete small language models; the answer is assembled locally.

This record is the integrated distribution. From version 3.0.0 this repository is the umbrella of the project: SwarmblyCore (protocol, specification, reference implementation, measurement harness and benchmark, formerly the whole repository), SwarmblyLCE (the Local Cognitive Extension, a memory that lives only on the user's device; own record 10.5281/zenodo.23289041) and SwarmblyApp (desktop client, peer-to-peer node and network monitor; own records under 10.5281/zenodo.23322638), at versions tested together and recorded in components.lock, with an interactive installer for macOS, Linux and Windows (quick or custom install).

Status: alpha. What is measured and what is not is stated in each component; the coherence-tax abandonment criterion is not met on its held-out test and the confidence map remains withdrawn. Licensing: software and specification under AGPL-3.0-or-later; document text under CC BY 4.0. The whitepaper (version 2) is deposited separately as 10.5281/zenodo.23031305.
notes: Defensive publication. The author asserts no patent claims over the disclosed techniques and places them in the public domain for patenting purposes. Elements E1-E18 are prior art from version 1.4 (10.5281/zenodo.21957088, 2026-08-14) and E19-E24 from version 2 (10.5281/zenodo.23031305, 2026-09-29); this distribution adds the integrated packaging of SwarmblyCore (with the swarmbly-agent runtime), SwarmblyLCE and SwarmblyApp, and the circle relay prototype, and does not withdraw any earlier element. Governance intent is documented in GOVERNANCE.md (Swiss Verein now, Stiftung later; DCO not CLA; no premine and no transferable token).
